previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with sudden-onset pain near her transplanted kidney, found to be due to persistent hydronephrosis despite a nephrostomy tube, which imaging showed was malpositioned. A nephrostogram confirmed ureteral obstruction, and a stent was successfully placed. Creatinine improved from 2.9 to 2.4 mg/dL. A kidney biopsy ruled out rejection but showed donor disease. The patient developed transient epigastric and referred pain, but cardiac workup was negative; symptoms were attributed to reflux, managed with omeprazole. Oral thrush was treated with nystatin. The nephrostomy tube was kept open due to low urine output when capped, likely from dehydration. She was discharged home stable, with instructions to continue linezolid, keep the tube open, monitor output, and follow up for labs and GI evaluation.

radiology_notes.text:
MEDICAL HISTORY:  ___ woman status post kidney transplant with
transplant ureteric stricture, status post transplant nephrostomy and
nephroureteric stent placement on ___.  Patient now presents with
leaking around the catheter and a request was placed for nephrostogram and
possible intervention.

COMPARISON:  NU stent placement performed on ___.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___.  Dr. ___
attending radiologist, was present and supervising throughout.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
100 mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of Versed throughout the total intraservice time
of 40 minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored.  Local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  An informed written consent was obtained after
explaining the procedure, benefits, alternatives and risks involved.  The
patient was brought to angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging
table.  The right lower quadrant including the existing catheter were prepped
and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Pre-procedure huddle and timeout
were performed as per ___ protocol.

An initial scout image of the right iliac fossa was obtained demonstrating a
kinked and malformed catheter in the expected location.  Dilute contrast
injection through the catheter demonstrated the catheter to have been pulled
back into one of the renal calyx.  The distal end was still into the urinary
bladder.  Given the above findings and leakage from the catheter, a decision
was made to exchange the NU stent for a new one.  The existing catheter was
cut distal to the hub to release the locking mechanism and removed over a
super stiff Glidewire.  The Glidewire was then exchanged for ___ wire
using a Kumpe catheter.  The tip of the wire was coiled in the urinary
bladder.  A new 8.5 ___ x 10 cm long Cook NU stent was placed over the
guidewire and the tip advanced into the bladder.  The guidewire and inner
plastic stiffener were then removed.  The bladder pigtail was noted to have
formed in the bladder and renal pigtail was formed in the pelvis and locked. 
Contrast injection through the newly placed catheter confirmed satisfactory
position and placement.  Nephrostogram also showed moderately hydronephrotic
collecting system with free passage of contrast through the catheter into the
urinary bladder.  Catheter was flushed and capped.  Catheter secured to the
skin with 0 silk suture and a StatLock device.  Sterile dressings were
applied.  The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Fluoroscopic scout image and nephrostogram through the existing catheter
demonstrated partially pulled out catheter with a malformed pigtail in the
calyx.
2.  The NU stent was successfully exchanged over a guidewire for a new 8.5
___ x 10 cm catheter with the renal pigtail positioned in the pelvis. 
Contrast injection through the newly placed catheter demonstrated no leakage
and satisfactory drainage into the urinary bladder.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  ___ female with end-stage renal disease status
post renal transplant.  The patient also is status post a new stent placement
with leaking around the stent and requires replacement.  This is the second
change from prior.

COMPARISON:  Last NU stent change dated ___.

2 mg of Versed and 150 mcg of fentanyl were administered in divided doses for
moderate conscious sedation.  Topical lidocaine gel was used for local
anesthesia.

PROCEDURE:
1.  Scout image.
2.  Tube injection through the indwelling NU stent.
3.  Nephrostogram through the sidearm of the sheath.
4.  Placement of a modified biliary drainage catheter with extra side holes as
a NU stent.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  A written informed consent was obtained explaining the
risks and benefits of the procedure.  The patient was brought to the
angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The indwelling
catheter at the skin around it was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion after a pre-procedure timeout and huddle per ___ protocol.

A scout image of the pelvis demonstrated the indwelling right sided NU stent,
which was kinked in the soft tissues proximal to the proximal pigtail.  The
distal pigtail also appears to be migrated.  Dilute contrast was injected
through the tube, which demonstrated opacification of the renal pelvis and the
calyces.  The proximal pigtail is within the lower calix and the distal
pigtail is migrated into the lower third of the ureter.  Opacification of the
bladder was also noted.  A ___ wire was then advanced through the
indwelling tube after cutting its hub and looped within the urinary bladder,
over which it was gently pulled out.  A 6 ___ 11 cm long ___ sheath
was then advanced over the wire with tip positioned in the renal calix and a
nephrostogram was performed which demonstrated normal opacification of the
renal pelvis and its calices.  Antegrade flow of contrast was noted slowly
from the renal pelvis into the ureter with gradual filling of the urinary
bladder.  We then used an 8 ___ Flexima biliary drainage
catheter and placed it over the wire and crossed across the ureter with the
pigtail within the urinary bladder.  A test injection here revealed that the
radiopaque marker was at the pelviureteric junction. The catheter was then
pulled back over the wire and extra side holes were cut and the catheter was
replaced over the wire and pigtailed within the urinary bladder.  Test
contrast injection was performed to demonstrate that the last side hole was
still within the renal collecting system and there was no contrast leakage
outside the kidney or in the ___ location.  Over two minutes, there was
complete emptying of the contrast from the renal collecting system into the
urinary bladder.  This catheter was secured to the skin with 0 silk sutures
and a StatLock.  It is connected to external bag for drainage.  Sterile
dressings were applied.  The patient withstood the procedure well and had no
immediate complications.

FINDINGS:
1.  Scout image demonstrating kink in the indwelling tube proximal to the
proximal pigtail.
2.  Tube injection demonstrating migrated proximal and distal pigtail loops.
3.  Nephrostogram demonstrating no evidence of hydronephrosis.  Gradual
emptying of the renal pelvis is noted.  The bladder is seen to opacify slowly.
4.  Tube injection performed via the modified NU stent demonstrating side
holes within the renal collecting system and pigtail in the bladder.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Nephrostogram performed demonstrating proximally migrated indwelling NU
stent.
2.  Placement of an 8 ___ modified NU stent optimally placed.
